note: ATV2 inference-pivot redesign pilot. 8 lectures x 4 pivots, exactly one inference/next-step pivot per lecture, redesigned on the symmetry principle: the four next-step options must each be the natural response to a DIFFERENT specific complication within the SAME study, comparably concrete and comparably scoped, not three generic research moves plus one downstream-of-thesis move. Fresh domains: Campanology, Ichthyology, Bryology, Vexillology, History of Cryptography, Malacology, Pomology, Runology -- none used in pilot, b1-b8 (incl. unfrozen b6-b8 drafts).

pivots.stem: What does the professor say the foundry's casting log recorded about the Ashcombe bell's first casting attempt?
settings: It cracked while cooling and had to be melted down within the week
It came out true, but noticeably lighter than the order specified
It came out sound, but had to be re-poured over an error in the founder's own inscription
It was cast successfully but delayed a full season by a shortage of tin

pivots.stem: Why does the professor mention the churchwarden's accounts from 1721?
settings: They record the parish's annual payment to the foundry for the bell's general upkeep
They show the tower was strengthened before the new bell arrived
They date a dispute between the parish and the founder over the delivery date
They list a smaller bell sold off to help pay for the new one

pivots.stem: What does the professor imply the conservation team will do with the bell's new laser scan?
settings: Compare the scan's acoustic model against the bell's actual recorded pitch
Use the scan to plan a low-vibration cradle for the bell's next transport
Use it to recreate the bell's profile for a replica cast elsewhere
Share the scan data with a neighbouring parish comparing bells from the same founder

pivots.stem: How does the professor respond to the claim that the bell's unusual tone comes from a flaw in its casting rather than its shape?
settings: She doubts it -- an identical flaw would show up in the foundry's other bells from that year, and none do
She leans toward accepting it, citing a slight unevenness recorded during the pour
She thinks the question is open, since both the shape and a casting flaw are still on the table
She rejects a casting flaw but allows the bell's shape may have shifted slightly as it aged

pivots.stem: What is the main point the professor wants to establish about the Corvane darter's migration?
settings: That the timing of the run is set by water temperature, not day length
That the population uses two distinct spawning grounds, not one
That the run has shifted three weeks later over the study's twenty years
That most of the run's mortality happens at a single culvert, not throughout the river

pivots.stem: What does the professor say the acoustic tags showed about fish that passed the culvert at night?
settings: They took nearly twice as long to clear it as fish that passed by day
They were no more likely to be lost from the record than daytime fish
They doubled back below the culvert far more often than daytime fish
They cleared it faster, but arrived at the spawning ground in poorer condition

pivots.stem: Why does the professor bring up the mill records from the 1920s?
settings: They fix the date the culvert was narrowed to its current width
They show the run was already present before the culvert existed
They record a flood that the professor uses to date a change in the channel
They document a much larger historical catch than today's population

pivots.stem: What does the professor imply the team will do about the culvert next season?
settings: Install a resting shelf partway up the culvert's inside wall
Move the acoustic receiver array further upstream to catch fish the culvert currently hides
Ask the mill's current owner for access to open the gate during the peak weeks
Tag a subset of fish with a longer-range transmitter to see where they go beyond the culvert

pivots.stem: What does the professor suggest the team will change about next year's plots on Hallow Moss?
settings: Fence two plots to keep deer off them and see whether growth recovers
Add a set of plots on the moss's shaded, north-facing edge for comparison
Move the growth measurement to a later date, since this year's readings ran early
Mark a fresh set of plots along the moss's eastern boundary, where last year's team never sampled

pivots.stem: How does the professor respond to the idea that trampling, not drainage, explains the moss's decline near the path?
settings: She is persuaded, since the decline stops abruptly at the same distance every year
She is doubtful, since drained plots far from any path show the same decline
She thinks both play a part but that the study cannot separate their shares
She rejects it outright, pointing to plots on the path that show no decline at all

pivots.stem: What does the professor say the water-table loggers recorded this year compared with the drought year five years ago?
settings: A shallower minimum, but for a longer stretch of the summer
A deeper minimum, reached in about half the time
Almost the same minimum, reached at almost the same date
A shallower minimum reached later, but recovering much faster in autumn

pivots.stem: Why does the professor mention the moss samples kept in the university herbarium since the 1950s?
settings: They let the team check whether today's moss is the same species as before
Their collection dates mark the last time the moss covered the whole bog
They record a decade when the moss was surveyed by a different, now-retired botanist
They show the moss was already a paler shade than field guides of the time describe

pivots.stem: Why does the professor mention Bruntsey Roads' 1888 pilot-boat log?
settings: It records the original height of the harbor's signal mast, later found to be inaccurate
It notes a shipment of replacement flags lost overboard before it ever reached the harbor
A damaged page in it dates a storm that later accounts disagree about
It lists the toll charged to fishing boats using the harbor's new pilot steps

pivots.stem: What does the professor imply the archive project will do with the newly found flag-maker's ledger?
settings: Match its handwriting against the harbor's own accounts to confirm which clerk kept it
Use its dye recipes to reproduce the original colors for the museum's replica set
Catalogue the ledger's flag-repair entries, which the harbor's own records never separately tracked
Cross-reference the ledger's order dates against the harbor's own light-keeper's diary

pivots.stem: What is the main point the professor wants to establish about the flag changeover?
settings: That it happened gradually, flag by flag, rather than on a single date
That it was driven by a naval order, not a local harbor decision
That the old and new codes were briefly used together on purpose
That confusion during the changeover caused at least one recorded near-collision

pivots.stem: How does the professor respond to the claim that Bruntsey's flagstaff design influenced the neighboring harbor's?
settings: She finds it plausible, mainly because the same carpenter is named in both harbors' accounts
She considers it an open question the surviving records cannot settle
She is unconvinced -- the neighboring harbor's staff predates Bruntsey's by several years
She agrees, but credits the shared merchant house rather than any direct copying

pivots.stem: What does the professor say the recovered key sheets showed about how often the Corvel cipher's substitution table changed?
settings: It changed every week, on a fixed schedule the clerks could predict
It changed only when a courier reported a sheet lost or compromised
It changed monthly, but the change was announced days later by a separate letter
It barely changed at all across the full run of years the sheets cover

pivots.stem: How does the professor respond to the claim that the Corvel cipher was broken by the rival trading company within its first year?
settings: She thinks it is unresolvable without letters the rival's archive no longer holds
She doubts it -- the rival's own letters keep making decisions the cipher would have prevented
She rejects it, but allows the rival broke a related, simpler cipher instead
She accepts it, based on a rival clerk's boast that survives in one letter

pivots.stem: What does the professor suggest the ongoing archive survey will let scholars do?
settings: Digitise the whole run before the fading ink makes any sheet unreadable
Fill the gap of substitution tables missing from the years the company fire affected
Establish which of the company's overseas offices received sheets first
Cross-check the sheets' paper stock against the company's known suppliers to help date the undated ones

pivots.stem: Why does the professor mention the ledger clerk's marginal doodles?
settings: One doodle turns out to be a partial key, copied down where it shouldn't be
They date the ledger to a specific quarter by referencing a known event
They show the clerk was distracted, which the professor uses to explain an error
They are unrelated, and the professor mentions them only as an aside

pivots.stem: How does the professor respond to the idea that boat traffic, not water quality, drove the Verrow limpet's decline?
settings: She rejects it, but allows boat wash may explain a separate, smaller local drop
She finds it convincing, since the sharpest drop follows the marina's opening
She is doubtful -- the decline began well before this stretch allowed any boats
She thinks the study cannot distinguish the two, since both changed together

pivots.stem: Why does the professor mention the water company's old filtration logs?
settings: They pin down the date a specific treatment change reached this stretch
They record a chemical spill nowhere else documented
They show the company monitored this species long before any survey did
They rule out a suspected upstream source of the runoff

pivots.stem: What does the professor say the shell-growth bands showed about limpets from the slower side-channel versus the main current?
settings: Side-channel limpets grew faster in most years but slower in drought years
Side-channel limpets grew steadily slower across every year in the record
The two groups grew at about the same rate until the last five years
Main-current limpets grew faster, but only in shells collected before the current logging equipment was installed

pivots.stem: What does the professor imply the team will do next to build on the filtration evidence?
settings: Place limpet cages just below the treatment outflow and monitor them through a full season
Send a batch of shells for isotope testing to see what the water carried when they grew
Ask the water company for the outflow's daily readings instead of the logged averages
Ask a neighbouring catchment's water company for its own filtration logs, to see whether the pattern repeats there

pivots.stem: What does the professor suggest the Marrow Hill orchard trust will do once the graft trial concludes?
settings: Release scion wood from the surviving grafts to other heritage orchards
Send wood samples from each surviving graft for a rootstock compatibility trial
Replant the trial block using only rootstock from the orchard's own oldest tree
Retire the trial's weakest grafts and free the block for a second generation of cuttings

pivots.stem: What does the professor say the trust's ledger recorded about the Coleraine seedling's original planting?
settings: It was the first tree in the orchard the trust ever fitted with a numbered tag
It was a gift tree, planted a decade after the rest of the orchard
It was the last tree planted before the orchard's boundary wall went up
It was moved once, early on, from a nursery row to its current spot

pivots.stem: How does the professor respond to the claim that the Coleraine seedling is a lost cultivar rediscovered, rather than a true original?
settings: She doubts it -- its fruit chemistry doesn't match any cultivar in the regional record
She rejects it, but agrees the tree was likely grafted onto older rootstock
She finds it plausible, given how closely its leaf shape matches one archived cultivar
She considers it undecidable without genetic testing the trust hasn't funded

pivots.stem: What is the main point the professor wants to establish about the Coleraine seedling's survival?
settings: That it survived the 1962 frost that killed most of the orchard's other trees
That it survived mainly because it stood apart from the blight that hit the rest
That its survival owes more to a caretaker's records than to the tree itself
That it very nearly did not survive a proposed grubbing in the 1980s

pivots.stem: Why does the professor mention the farmer's account of moving the Hollowmere stone in 1911?
settings: It explains why the stone's base no longer matches its original socket
It is the only record placing the stone at its present site before 1950
It preserves a detail about a second, smaller stone since lost
It fixes the date of a churchyard clearance the stone's current plinth was built for

pivots.stem: What does the professor say the new raking-light photographs showed about the stone's final line?
settings: Traces of a name where earlier readings had seen only an ornamental border
That the line was added later, in a noticeably different hand
That what earlier readers took for damage was in fact a deliberate erasure
A short phrase that matches a formula found on two other stones in the region

pivots.stem: How does the professor respond to the claim that the Hollowmere stone commemorates a voyage rather than a death?
settings: She rejects it, but agrees the named river points to an unusually well-traveled family
She doubts it -- the stone's opening line names the deceased using a formula reserved for burials
She thinks the text alone cannot settle it, and no other evidence survives
She finds it plausible, since the stone's carving style matches others raised for departures rather than deaths

pivots.stem: What does the professor imply the runology project will do once the raking-light survey of the region is complete?
settings: Cross-match the stone's line breaks against the region's known scribal training centres
Ask a stonemasons' guild archive whether any apprentice records mention working on this stone
Compare the stone's carving depth against weathering-rate data from other markers at the same site
Send a cast of the stone's final line to a specialist in a neighbouring kingdom's script for a second opinion
